biography.plain_text: Bernard Tapie was a French entrepreneur who built his fortune by buying and restructuring struggling companies, including Wonder and Terraillon. He later owned Adidas, presided over Olympique de Marseille and served as a government minister. His business career was marked by insolvency and a prolonged dispute over the Adidas sale.

confidence.reason: Primary parliamentary biography, civil ownership history and contemporary reporting support the defining business and public roles.

long_biography.plain_text:
Entrepreneur Bernard Tapie made starting a business the subject of his television programme Ambitions. In its first broadcast, he guided a young woman's composting proposal through marketing advice, legal questions and a financing panel. Viewers could telephone to offer engineers, sales staff or distribution help, turning the programme into a public recruitment pitch.

He also financed sales-training schools for young people without conventional qualifications or work. The network reached six establishments in France, Belgium and Switzerland. Courses were intensive and geared towards commercial careers. Funded from his own resources, the schools closed when his finances collapsed in 1994.
